candidates.title: Graduate Program
candidates.abstract: Our Graduate Program offers hands-on experience, professional development, mentoring and exposure to a range of projects that make a real difference.
bullets: Free your degree to build strong and connected communities
Build new ways to engage locally within a diverse and dynamic team
Work where creativity meets care – for people, place and purpose
candidates.content_text:
The City of Charles Sturt is excited to recruit 3 x Graduates to join our Graduate Program.
This is your opportunity to put your qualification into practice, gain valuable workplace experience, and build a meaningful career with one of South Australia's most progressive and community-focused councils.
Our two-year Graduate Program offers hands-on experience, professional development, mentoring, and exposure to a wide range of projects that make a real difference to our community.
Whether your passion lies in people, community, engineering, planning, technology, business, communications, environment, governance, or another professional discipline, we want to help you turn your qualification into a rewarding career.
We're looking for curious, motivated and community-minded graduates who are ready to learn, contribute and grow while helping shape the future of the City of Charles Sturt.
 About the role:
As a Graduate, you will be placed within a Division that aligns with your skills, qualifications and career aspirations.
Depending on your background, you may work across areas such as:
 - Customer Experience
 - Community Development
 - Community Health and Safety
 - Communications and Engagement
 - Finance
 - Human Resources
 - Planning and Environment
 - Engineering and Infrastructure
 - Technology and Digital Services
 - Data and Analytics
 - Performance, Business Intelligence and Improvement
 - Governance and Risk
Throughout the program you will:
 - Contribute to meaningful projects that deliver real community outcomes
 - Gain exposure to different areas of local government
 - Build professional, technical and leadership skills
 - Receive mentoring, coaching and development opportunities
 - Expand your professional network across Council
 - Develop a strong understanding of how local government serves and supports communities
Our flexible approach means each graduate's experience will be unique and tailored to maximise learning, development and career opportunities.
This immersive approach ensures you develop a deep understanding of local government operations while building the skills and confidence to grow a successful and impactful career.
About You: 
We are seeking a progressive and well-rounded graduate to join us. You are enthusiastic, curious and ready to make a positive contribution.
You may be a recent graduate or in the final stages of completing your studies and are looking for an opportunity to launch your professional career.
You will demonstrate:
 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills
 - A willingness to learn and embrace new challenges
 - Initiative and sound problem-solving skills
 - An ability to work collaboratively with others
 - A passion for improving outcomes for communities
 - A desire to build a long-term career and develop professionally
Qualifications:
We encourage applications from graduates who have completed, or are due to complete, a tertiary qualification in a relevant discipline, including but not limited to:
 - Business, Commerce and Finance
 - Information Technology, Digital and Data Analytics
 - Engineering, Infrastructure and Asset Management
 - Planning, Environment and Sustainability
 - Community Development and Social Sciences
 - Human Resources, Psychology and Organisational Development
 - Communications, Marketing and Public Relations
 - Project Management and Business Improvement
 - GIS, Spatial and Geospatial Sciences
 - Other disciplines relevant to local government.
Applicants with qualifications in other relevant disciplines are also encouraged to apply.
About Our Organisation: 
The City of Charles Sturt is a vibrant community home to around 130,000 people across 105 different cultures. We champion unity in diversity and strive to reflect our community within our workforce - wherever you are from, you are home in the City of Charles Sturt.
We prioritise customer and employee experience and a supportive environment where everyone belongs. With over 500 employees, our people and our community "Means the World" to us which highlights the importance of our places, our people and our service to the community.
The Detail: 
A graduate employee will enjoy:
 - A full-time, fixed-term contract for a period of two years
 - Starting salary from $86,219.09 per annum + Superannuation + Annual Leave Loading.
To be considered for this opportunity, you must have unrestricted work rights in Australia for the duration of this contract. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. 
How to Apply:
Click ‘Apply for this job’ to submit your application for this vacancy by, 5.00pm, Monday, 12 October 2026. Provide us with your resume, as well as answering the following questions:
1. Why would you like to join the City of Charles Sturt Graduate Program?
2. What strengths, skills or experiences would you bring as a graduate?
3. Which study discipline did you complete and what areas of local government most interest you?
4. What do you hope to gain from participating in the Graduate Program?
For further information about this opportunity, please view the attached position description. 
Enquiries about this position may be made to the following:
Kristen Gigante - People Engagement and Capability Lead
kgigante@charlessturt.sa.gov.au 
IMPORTANT: For optimal performance, please use Chrome, Safari or Edge in order to apply for this opportunity. Should you encounter issues uploading your cover letter or resume at the application stage, please re-try your application through Chrome.- Position Description - Graduate Program

candidates.title: Cadet Project Officer
candidates.abstract: Join Lake Mac as a Cadet Project Officer and gain practical experience, professional mentoring, and support to complete your studies!
bullets: Payment of your university tuition fees and student amenities fees
A 35-hour working week with a 9-day fortnight
Access to a wide range of employee health, wellbeing and lifestyle benefits
candidates.content_text:
Term Contact: Up to 6 years
Qualifications: studying a Bachelor of Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Architecture, Planning, or another related discipline
Salary: starting from $1,153.93 to $1,322.76 per week plus 12% superannuation
Commencing: January 2027
Ready to launch your career in Engineering, Construction Management, Planning, Architecture, Project Management or another related discipline? Join Lake Macquarie City Council as a Cadet Project Officer and gain practical experience, professional mentoring, and support to complete your studies while making a real difference in our community.
ABOUT THE JOB
Kick-start your career while completing your studies with a hands-on Cadetship that combines paid work, professional mentoring, and university learning. Throughout the program, you'll gain valuable experience delivering community infrastructure projects that make a real difference to our region. You'll work alongside experienced professionals across our Project Delivery, Engineering, and Quality & Surveillance teams, building practical skills in project management, construction, contract administration, stakeholder engagement, and infrastructure delivery.
In this role, you'll:
- Contribute to the delivery of community infrastructure projects.
- Gain experience in project planning, procurement and contract management.
- Work with consultants, contractors and project teams.
- Assist with technical research, reporting, and project documentation.
- Learn how projects are delivered safely, sustainably, on time and within budget.
- Develop knowledge of quality assurance, compliance and regulatory processes.
- Build your professional skills through mentoring, training and real-world experience.
WHAT WE OFFER
- Payment of your university tuition fees and student amenities fees for the remainder of your approved undergraduate studies!
- Paid study leave and time to attend compulsory classes, helping you successfully balance work and university commitments
- Hands-on experience working on real planning projects that help shape our community
- Ongoing mentoring and support from experienced planning professionals
- A structured learning and development pathway to help you build a successful career
- Annual salary reviews and progression opportunities based on performance
- A 35-hour working week with a 9-day fortnight, giving you more time for life outside work
- Four weeks of paid annual leave each year
- A supportive, collaborative and innovative team environment where your ideas are valued
- Access to a wide range of employee health, wellbeing and lifestyle benefits – click here for more.
ABOUT YOU
We're looking for a motivated and enthusiastic student who is passionate about shaping communities and building a career in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Project Management, Planning, or a related field.
To be successful in this role, you'll:
- Be eligible to enrol in the second year (or later year) of a relevant Bachelor's degree in 2027, such as Engineering, Architecture, Construction, Planning, or a related discipline.
- Have strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build positive relationships with a variety of people.
- Demonstrate problem-solving skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Be comfortable using Microsoft Office applications and other digital systems.
- Have an interest in infrastructure delivery, project management, design, construction, or community development.
- Be committed to completing the study and training requirements of the cadetship.
- Enjoy working collaboratively as part of a supportive and high-performing team.
- Hold a White Card (NSW General Construction Induction), or be willing to obtain one.
- Hold a minimum Provisional Driver Licence.
The position is based in Speers Point; however, the initial work location will be Council's temporary Administration Building in Wallsend, unless otherwise advised. The role will also involve travel throughout the Lake Macquarie local government area.
Read the Position Statement and Capability Framework to learn more about this exciting opportunity.
Candidates who have already completed a degree-level qualification or higher in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Architecture, Planning, or another relevant discipline are not eligible to apply.
HOW TO APPLY
If this job sounds like you, we would love to hear from you! Get your application in by midnight, Monday 12 October 2026.
- Check out the FAQs and Guide to Applying before starting your application.
- Click the ‘Apply Now’ button below to start your application. You will need to upload a resume and provide responses to application questions based on the position statement.
- Please see the attached recruitment timeline, which outlines the key dates and activities for the recruitment process. We recommend downloading and saving a copy for future reference.
We welcome and encourage applications from all ages and genders, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally diverse backgrounds, the LGBTIQ+ community, refugees, and people with disability. We understand the skills and attributes veterans can bring to our Council.
As part of the recruitment process, prior to an offer of employment being made, recommended candidates may be subject to a medical assessment which may include alcohol and other drugs testing.

candidates.title: Graduate Engineer - Project Delivery
candidates.abstract: Build project delivery skills that shape communities.
bullets: Work on real projects that shape your future.
Fixed-term Full-time position
Flexible working arrangements
candidates.content_text:
City of Newcastle is seeking a motivated Graduate Engineer – Project Manager to join our Project Delivery team and build practical experience while contributing to projects that shape our city. 
This graduate position provides recent graduates with the opportunity to develop professional skills, apply academic knowledge in a practical workplace environment, and contribute to meaningful projects and operational activities across City of Newcastle. 
Working within the Project Delivery team for the duration of the engagement, you will support the management and timely delivery of a range of capital works projects that enhance existing assets and deliver new infrastructure for the Newcastle community. Under the direction of the Manager Projects, you will gain exposure to project delivery, contract documentation, stakeholder engagement, research, analysis and continuous improvement activities. 
Through hands-on experience across infrastructure and asset-related projects, you will build organisational knowledge and develop capabilities that support your future career growth and assist with co-creating our city.
Find out more about your new career by viewing the position description here.
Life at City of Newcastle (CN) 
You’ll get to experience your work up close alongside the brilliant minds of your colleagues who care for one another and the region. 
You’ll chip away at ambitious plans with a talented, passionate crew alongside you, shaping the very fabric of our community. Showing up for neighbours not shareholders. 
Every single day offers the chance to think big and act local. Planning and prioritising to achieve the most important outcomes with the community. 
You’ll add value in the moments that matter. From librarians to lifeguards, in a range of iconic places, we achieve a better Newcastle together. 
Whether we’re planning to host major events, providing essential services or supporting creative artists, it’s what we do when the cameras aren't rolling that matters most. 
And we’ll be there for you in important times in your life. We embrace flexible work arrangements to find a balance that allows us to enjoy the city we shape. 
Our focus on inclusion and respecting culture, will help you feel a deeper connection with others. You'll connect with internal communities that will help you to feel a sense of belonging and reflect the diversity of the growing region. 
You’ll do meaningful work and do it sustainably as you take ideas from plan to play, in your own backyard.
With hundreds of different roles, each person adds their uniqueness to our culture and plays their part as we head towards our 2040 vision. 
With natural assets and a focus on the environment, co-create a sustainable region with us. 
Why join CN? 
At CN, we value our employees, and their wellbeing takes priority. We encourage employees to make time for what's important and provide the benefits to enable a work life balance that allow us to enjoy the city we shape. To read more, visit here!
- 35-hour working week with flexible/hybrid work arrangements/model as well as an optional 9-day fortnight 
- 4 weeks of annual leave, 3 weeks of personal leave plus 2 additional paid public holidays 
- 17.5% annual leave loading yearly payment 
- Paid parental leave for primary carers 
- Industry leading employment conditions 
- Corporate Fitness program from as little as $18.00 per fortnight
- Access to a range of exclusive CN employee benefits programs including Novated Lease options as well as access to reward and recognition vouchers 
- Annual performance development plans and ongoing training and development opportunities 
- Leading the CN Way leadership program 
- Inclusion, Diversity & Equity (IDE) employee networks and initiatives 
- Access to Health & Wellbeing programs including an Onsite Physiotherapist and Psychology, Yoga and Mental Health Ambassador Groups 
We champion inclusion so that everyone is valued, and we encourage innovation and creativity. We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive workplace where different styles, backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are valued, encouraged, and respected. 
People with diverse lived experiences (including but not limited to, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians, people with diverse gender identities and sexualities, people from different cultural, racial, ethnic, religious and linguistic backgrounds, people with disability, carers, and veterans) are encouraged to apply. 
Don’t just work for the city, co-create it. Join and expand your career at the City of Newcastle. 
What is next? 
If you are shortlisted you will be required to attend 1 x group assessment centre for a 3-hour period to be held the week of 2nd Nov 2026.
Application Closing Date: Saturday 17 October 2026
Remuneration:  $88,889.29 + 17.5% annual leave loading yearly payment + 12% Superannuation per annum for a 35-hour week
Contact: Melissa Moore - Career Ready Advisor – 02 4974 1377
If you need any adjustments to be made to the recruitment process or if you would like to discuss any accessibility requirements, please contact recruit@ncc.nsw.gov.au for a confidential discussion.

candidates.title: 2027 Engineering Drafting Traineeship - Hort Enterprises, Orange NSW
candidates.abstract: Earn while you learn and build real-world engineering and CAD skills!
candidates.location: Orange, Blue Mountains & Central West NSW
bullets: Hands-on Training with Industry Experts
Pathway to a Secure and Rewarding Career
Supportive work culture
screening_questions: Do you have a current Australian driver's licence?
Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
I have read and understood the Privacy Policy and consent to the collection, use and disclosure of my personal information as described
candidates.content_text:
About Hort Enterprises
Hort Enterprises is a locally owned and operated engineering company with more than 30 years of industry experience. What began as an engineering support business for the agricultural sector has grown into a leading engineering operation servicing mining and industrial clients across Australia. 
This is an exciting opportunity to start your career with a well-respected local employer and learn from an experienced team with a wealth of industry knowledge. The workplace is described as fun, supportive, collaborative and outgoing, with Hort ideally looking to retain the successful trainee following completion of the traineeship.
To learn more about Hort Enterprises, visit: www.horts.au
About the Traineeship
Are you finishing school, recently graduated, or looking to kick-start your career in engineering and design?
Hort Enterprises is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic individual to join their Orange team as an Engineering Drafting Trainee. 
This opportunity is ideal for someone with an interest in engineering, design, technology, maths and computers who would like to develop a practical career within the engineering industry. 
Working alongside experienced staff, you’ll gain practical exposure to engineering drafting, CAD software, detailed drawings, site scoping, measuring and 3D laser scanning while developing valuable technical and workplace skills. The successful candidate will complete a Certificate IV in Engineering Drafting.
What You’ll Learn
This traineeship is all about learning on the job, gaining real experience and building skills you can take with you throughout your career.
With support from experienced professionals, you’ll:
- Prepare detailed engineering drawings using industry-standard CAD software
- Understand steelwork fabrication and machining processes
- Assist with customer site scoping and taking precise measurements
- Utilise modern 3D laser scanning technology
- Apply Microsoft Office programs and specialised CAD systems
- Gain practical mechanical knowledge and collaborating closely with design professionals
Who We’re Looking For
We encourage applications from people who:
- Have an interest in engineering, drafting, design and technology
- Possess sound knowledge of computer skills
- Enjoy maths and practical problem-solving
- Have good mechanical aptitude
- Are reliable and able to manage their time effectively
- Communicate clearly and can follow instructions
- Are comfortable providing good customer service
- Have practical skills and are keen to learn
- Are comfortable with the possibility of travel to customer sites, including remote and underground locations
- Are willing to undergo a pre-employment medical screening and National Police Check
Why Choose a Traineeship with Hort Enterprises?
- Earn while you learn
- Develop practical engineering drafting and CAD skills
- Learn from experienced staff with a wealth of industry knowledge
- Gain exposure to real engineering projects
- Work within a fun, supportive and collaborative team
- Build valuable technical, practical and customer-facing skills
- Opportunity for ongoing employment, with Hort Enterprises ideally looking for the successful candidate to stay on following completion of the traineeship 
Ready to Start Your Career?
If you’re interested in engineering, drafting, design or technology and want to turn those interests into a career, this could be the opportunity for you.
Students, recent school leavers and applicants looking to begin a long-term career in the engineering industry are encouraged to apply.
How to apply
- Click the APPLY NOW button or visit https://skillset.com.au/job-vacancies/ 
- Submit your application, including a Resume and Cover Letter 
- If you have completed any relevant school projects, work experience, metalwork, engineering, woodworking, welding, or other practical projects, we'd love to see them. Please include photos, certificates, reports, or a portfolio (if applicable)
- If you require further information, please contact Skillset for a confidential discussion on 1300 853 525 
About Skillset
At Skillset, we create life-changing opportunities for people and communities across regional NSW. With over 42 years of experience, we provide recruitment, apprenticeship, and traineeship services, as well as mentoring and skills development. We are committed to helping individuals achieve their goals and supporting businesses to succeed.
Skillset Youth Connect is a free service that works with 15- to 21-year-olds not in school or work, to plan and achieve the training and career goals that are suited to them.
Click on the link below to learn more:
https://skillset.com.au/employment-career-development/youth-career-counselling/

screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?

candidates.content_text:
About ABI Civil Contracting NSW
ABI Civil Contracting NSW is a progressive Australian civil contractor delivering major infrastructure projects across NSW and the ACT.
Our diverse project portfolio includes transport infrastructure, bridges, utilities, renewable energy, substations, data centres, defence and major commercial civil works.
Due to continued growth, we are seeking a Project Engineer to join our project delivery team.
The Opportunity
Reporting to the Project Manager, the successful candidate will be responsible for supporting the delivery of civil construction projects, coordinating engineering activities and ensuring works are completed safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
We are seeking an individual who can demonstrate previous experience working as a Project Engineer within the civil construction industry and has a proven ability to contribute to successful project outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate day-to-day engineering activities.
- Manage technical queries, subcontractors and project interfaces.
- Monitor project progress, quality and compliance requirements.
- Assist with procurement, project reporting and contract administration.
- Support a strong safety and quality culture.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Civil Engineering degree or equivalent qualification.
- Demonstrated experience working as a Project Engineer within civil construction (8+ years).
- Strong understanding of project delivery, documentation and contract administration.
- Excellent communication and organisational skills.
- A proactive attitude and commitment to achieving project o
Experience across roads, bridges, rail, utilities, renewable energy, substations, data centres, defence or commercial civil projects will be highly regarded.
What We Offer:
- Competitive salary package
- Opportunity to work on diverse and challenging infrastructure projects
- Career development with a growing civil contractor

candidates.title: Intern Drafter
candidates.abstract: Support Senior Drafters and Engineers in technical drawings and CAD drafting.
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a draftsperson?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
candidates.content_text:
About the Company
Menard Oceania is a design and construct specialist geotechnical contractor offering expertise in ground improvement and reinforcement for sites with poor soils. Its treatments eliminate the need for the deep foundations traditionally used to support surface structures. Our scope includes small to large infrastructure-based solutions across a broad range of market segments for private and public stakeholders, including Transport, Dams, Ports and Coastal Infrastructure, Industrial and Commercial Buildings, Heavy Industry and Mining.
Your Role
The Intern drafting Assistant will support the senior drafting & design engineers in the preparation, modification, and coordination of civil, structural and geotechnical engineering drawings and documentation. This position provides an opportunity to develop technical drafting expertise and engineering knowledge while working within a collaborative project team.
Skills and Qualifications
- Basic knowledge of engineering drawing standards and principles.
- Basic proficiency in AutoCAD; Civil 3D experience is advantageous.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Key Attributes
- Detail-oriented with a strong focus on quality and precision.
- Eager to learn and develop technical drafting and engineering knowledge.
- Organised and capable of managing multiple tasks effectively.
- Positive team player with a proactive approach to supporting project delivery.
Training & Development 
On-the-Job Training and Development
The role provides structured on-the-job training and mentoring from experienced Senior Draft’s person and the Design Manager. The successful candidate will receive hands-on guidance in engineering drafting practices, project delivery processes, and the application of industry standards across civil, structural, and geotechnical engineering disciplines.
Salary & Benefits
Remuneration will be competitive with current market rates, depending on qualifications and experience.
Applicants must have full working rights in Australia to be considered for this position

candidates.title: Graduate Engineer
candidates.abstract: Looking to build strong technical foundations in compliance-focused engineering — with real industry exposure from day one? We’d love to hear from you
bullets: Five weeks annual leave
Food provided for staff lunches
Experience in a high demand niche
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?

candidates.content_text:
Company Overview
Based in Brisbane, Snap Fire Systems is an industry leader in passive fire protection, renowned for our commitment to innovation, research and development, and unwavering integrity. We are constantly pushing the boundaries to maintain and enhance our market-leading position, and we're seeking a motivated engineering graduate to join our close-knit team.
The passive fire protection industry is a specialized and rapidly growing field worldwide. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain experience that is difficult to find elsewhere. With the rise in high-rise developments globally, this position provides invaluable exposure to the intersection of theoretical knowledge, product performance, regulatory standards, and practical construction industry challenges. This expertise is highly valued by leading building companies, certifiers, manufacturers, and test laboratories.
Snap Fire Systems proudly manufactures and distributes cutting-edge passive fire protection products across Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom. Our company is recognized for its innovation, market leadership, and exceptional customer support.
General Role Description
- Assist in the design and development of new products
- Material research
- Work alongside the R&D team testing new products
- Manage and optimise datasets
- Liaising with external test facilities to manage test and assessment programs
- Answer phone and email technical enquiries
Prerequisites
·         Full and unrestricted working rights in Australia, with no requirement for employer sponsorship, either now or in the future.
·         Availability to work full-time on an ongoing basis.
·         A genuine commit to the role on a long-term basis.
Preferred Requirements
- Bachelor’s in Mechanical/Structural Engineering or similar qualification in fire safety engineering.
- Previous experience in a similar technical role
- Experience in the construction industry
- Demonstrated ability to innovate, show initiative and logically analyse
- Strong CAD proficiency
- Strong Excel skills
- Excellent communication skills
- Proactive, and willingness to learn
- Attention to detail and accuracy
- Ability to work unsupervised at times
- Ability and willingness to meet deadlines
What We Offer
- Five weeks annual leave
- Low stress work environment
- Exciting position in a growing company
- Flexible working arrangements
- Food provided for staff lunches
- Experience in a high demand niche 
- Exposure to the construction industry
- Off street parking
You will be provided with all the business tools you need to be successful in the role and a salary package will be negotiated after the short list process.

candidates.title: Junior Technical Officer
candidates.abstract: Service Stream’s Radhaz division currently seek a Junior Technical Officer to join us at an exciting stage of our journey!
bullets: Launch your engineering career in a growing ASX-listed company
Build hands-on expertise in RF modelling, EME compliance and field work
Grow your skills with training, career pathways & long-term opportunities!
candidates.content_text:
Service Stream’s Radhaz division are specialists within Electromagnetic Emissions (EME) Measurement, compliance and consulting services and currently seek a Junior Technical Officer to come onboard! 
Reporting directly to the Technical Services Manager, you will be responsible for producing detailed EME drawings and compliance documentation for various customers including telecommunications carriers, radio service operators, site owners, consultants and designers. 
This is a permanent, full-time role, working within a likeable team, based in Clayton South. It's also the perfect opportunity for a recent Engineering graduate, who is wanting to start their career off with a growing and diverse ASX-listed company, known for offering a number of long-term benefits and opportunities.
Key Responsibilities:
- Use proprietary software to model and map RF EME levels emitted from antennas
- Prepare site compliance documentation in various formats
- Maintain both in-house and external web-based databases
- Liaise with clients, manufacturers and others as required to gather information
- Assist with project management, quoting and job costing
- Undertake field work including site inspections/audits and basic RF EME measurements
- Work in accordance with the Radhaz QMS, including NATA accreditation requirements and Service Stream SSM Integrated Management Systems (QA and OHS&E)
- Any other reasonable day to day tasks & duties as required
Skills and Experience:
- Tertiary qualifications within Engineering
- Ability to project coordinate, manage and multi-task as required.
- Understanding of technical drawings
- Radio frequency field modelling and measurement techniques
- Red card/white card and working at heights as required for field work
Benefits of this role & working with us:
Kick-start your career - Leverage your engineering studies & skills with a growing ASX-listed company
Career development – we offer growth opportunities and support internal mobility. You will have access to skill enhancement through our online learning system and onsite training.
Access - discounts for hundreds of businesses such as Woolworths, Air BNB, The Iconic, JB HI-FI, Dan Murphys, Bupa Health Care, and Specsavers. We also offer access to novated leasing and a share matching program.
Paid leave - parental, cultural, community service, defence, study, corporate volunteering and purchased leave available.
Culture – we are dedicated to fostering a workplace environment that values diversity and inclusion, and meaningful recognition. You will play a key role in building the culture of our new team.
Service Stream is an equal opportunity employer who believes diversity of thought, background and experience strengthens relationships and benefits our people, clients and communities.
We are committed to cultivate an inclusive and high-performing culture where our people thrive and are proud to bring their whole selves to work, inspiring a respectful and inclusive environment.
Service Stream encourages and welcomes the opportunity for applicants to share their lived experiences.

candidates.content_text:
Company description:
.
Job description:
Make it yours. 
Experience the excitement of building a career in an evolving construction business where people and performance make amazing things happen. 
Who we are
We're Davison, Symal's South Australian civil construction business, backed by the strength, scale and self-performing capability of the wider Symal Group.
Built on the legacy of Davison Earthmovers, our team brings nearly four decades of local experience delivering earthmoving and civil works.
We combine local relationships, a skilled South Australian workforce and proven delivery in earthworks, civil construction, and defence. Together, we're building on Davison's proud history while creating new opportunities for our people, clients and communities across South Australia.
The role: 
As our Project Engineer, you'll play a key role in delivering diverse civil projects across Adelaide, from earthworks and drainage to gaining experience in defence projects. You'll work closely with experienced leaders, take ownership of meaningful project outcomes, and build your career in a growing South Australian business backed by the strength of Symal Group.
Your impact: 
You'll bring hands-on experience to a team that values efficiency and quality. Together, we'll deliver projects that run smoothly, finish on time and make a real difference to the communities we work in.
Your every day: 
 - Coordinating and administering construction engineering activities to ensure that projects are delivered in accordance with plans, designs and specifications.
 - Participating in monthly financial reviews and providing cost forecasts against budgets to understand cost to complete.
 - Leading and supporting a strong safety culture.
 - Managing the construction program and implementing mitigating measures to keep the program on track.
 - Demonstrating financial awareness and industry understanding when contributing to project decisions.
 Who are you? 
 - Bachelor's degree in civil engineering or equivalent is preferred 
 - Hold Australian Citizenship or Permanent Residency
 - Engineering experience on a broad range of civil projects such as road, earthworks, drainage, land division and infrastructure
 - Sound understanding of the local construction industry and familiarity with contractors, councils and clients
 - Excellent stakeholder management experience
 - Current South Australian Drivers Licence 
 A career with us 
Symal is an equal opportunity employer. Our teams are made up of individuals with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, with aligned ways of working, enabling us to overcome any challenge, advance our careers and outperform competitors. 
Staff perks and benefits offered to build an engaged and talented workforce include: 
 - Tailored professional development opportunities for career advancement  
 - Opportunities to work on a wide variety of exciting and complex projects  
 - Bonus leave days, including your birthday off 
 - Hundreds of discounts at leading retailers with our employee perk program 
 We're committed to ensuring that our recruitment process is fair, inclusive, free from bias and accessible for all candidates. 
We are an inclusive workplace and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, veterans, and individuals from diverse cultural and life experiences are encouraged to apply.
